text: complex-survey data (NHANES, PISA, …), pass sampling-weight column via sampling_weights. Survey weights lme4 weights= (precision weights), fit routes WeMix::mix() – weighted pseudo-maximum-likelihood (Rabe-Hesketh & Skrondal 2006) – engine = "lme4" sampling weights error rather silent misfit. Limitations: wemix engine covers canonical gaussian(identity) / binomial(logit) MAIHDA single (1 | stratum) intercept. crossed random effects (context =, decomposition = "crossed-dimensions") bootstrap intervals require lme4/brms. design-based interval need replicate weights, upcoming future extension.
code: # One call: design-weighted null + adjusted models and PCV. The engine switches # to "wemix" automatically (install WeMix from CRAN). analysis <- maihda(   outcome ~ age + (1 | gender:race:education),   data = survey_data,   sampling_weights = "person_weight" ) analysis            # design-weighted VPC/ICC and PCV summary(analysis)   # design-consistent (sandwich) SEs for the fixed effects  # Works across the toolkit: stepwise PCV, group comparison, prediction, plots, # and the design-weighted AUC for binary outcomes. stepwise_pcv(strata_data, "outcome", c("gender", "race", "education"),              sampling_weights = "person_weight")  # Bayesian alternative: weights enter as likelihood weights (pseudo-posterior -- # point estimates are design-consistent; credible intervals are not design-based). fit_maihda(outcome ~ age + (1 | gender:race:education), data = survey_data,            engine = "brms", sampling_weights = "person_weight")

text: Computes variance partition coefficient response (probability) scale binomial MAIHDA model, using simulation method Goldstein, Browne & Rasbash (2002). Stratum random effects \(u \sim N(0, \sigma^2_u)\) simulated converted predicted probabilities \(p = g^{-1}(\eta + u)\) (\(\eta\) fixed-part linear predictor); VPC -stratum variance \(p\) share total (+ binomial within-stratum variance \(\overline{p(1-p)}\)). Unlike latent-scale VPC (fixed level-1 variance \(\pi^2/3\) logit), response-scale VPC depends overall outcome prevalence, report complement – replacement – latent-scale value.
